avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin/Anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and displace warfarin from protein binding, significantly increasing bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if necessary, require INR monitoring and dose adjustment by prescriber

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Combined antiplatelet effects increase bleeding risk, particularly with NSAIDs
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin E to <400 IU daily or avoid supplementation; monitor for signs of bleeding

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Ginkgo potentiates antiplatelet effects of NSAIDs, increasing hemorrhage risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; counsel patient to discontinue ginkgo before starting nabumetone

caution_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose supplements)
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects that could additively affect NSAID-induced platelet inhibition
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased bruising or bleeding; consider limiting supplemental garlic intake

caution_supplements.name: Licorice
caution_supplements.mechanism: May promote sodium retention and hypertension, compounding NSAID-related fluid retention
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; use lowest effective nabumetone dose and maintain adequate hydration

avoid_foods.name: Alcohol (>2 drinks daily)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Alcohol increases gastric irritation and GI bleeding risk; both nabumetone and alcohol impair platelet function
avoid_foods.action: Advise patient to limit alcohol to ≤1 drink/day or avoid completely; counsel on GI bleed warning signs

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods/salt
caution_foods.mechanism: NSAIDs promote sodium retention and fluid accumulation; excess dietary sodium increases hypertension and edema risk
caution_foods.action: Recommend moderate salt restriction; monitor weight and blood pressure regularly

caution_foods.name: Fatty/fried foods
caution_foods.mechanism: May delay nabumetone absorption and increase GI upset when combined with NSAIDs
caution_foods.action: Take nabumetone with food to reduce GI irritation, but avoid heavy fatty meals immediately before/after dosing

monitoring_notes: Monitor renal function, blood pressure, and for signs of GI bleeding (dark stools, abdominal pain, hematemesis). Nabumetone is less selective for COX-1 inhibition than some NSAIDs but still carries substantial cardiovascular, renal, and GI risks, particularly in patients >65 years or with comorbid conditions.
